newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Fidelity sees strong growth in Swiss fund market.
newsitem.headline: Fidelity sees strong growth in Swiss fund market.

text.p: Fidelity Investment Services, one of the biggest mutual fund companies in the world with $520 billion in assets under management, reported strong growth in the number of clients in the expanding Swiss market.

Fidelity official Sophie Launay said new clients in Switzerland accounted for an important part of the growth in net flows to Fidelity's Luxembourg-listed fund to $6 billion in June from $5 billion at end-1996 and $4 billion in February 1996.
The fund is listed as a SICAV.

The Swiss mutual fund market, where foreign investors mainly from continental Europe as well as emerging markets make up the bulk of clients, has whetted the appetite of foreign groups including Flemings and Citibank.
The latest newcomer is Templeton Emerging Market Funds, whose president Mark Mobius announced plans this month to open an office in Zurich.
Launay declined to give the share of Swiss-based clients in Fidelity's Luxembourg fund, whose annual growth in 1997 is expected to nearly double last year's 25 percent, she said.
"We are seeing good growth in the Swiss market where we are more active. We are planning to expand," she said.
Many Swiss banks are seeking innovative niches on the Swiss mutual fund market, where net inflows grew by 26 percent in 1996 according to Swiss fund statistician Bopp ISB.
